newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese bought U.S. bonds actively in August -MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japanese bought U.S. bonds actively in August -MOF.

text.p: Japanese investors' heavy investment in U.S. Treasury bonds was a major factor pushing up investors' net purchases of foreign bonds in August, a Finance Ministry official said on Wednesday.

Net purchases of U.S. Treasuries by Japanese investors totalled 696.0 billion yen in August, the largest amount since July 1995, when they were at 776.9 billion. Net purchases amounted to 264.3 billion yen in July.
"Investment in U.S. Treasury bonds was large and that pushed up the overall net buying figures," the official told reporters.

The official said the volume of net U.S. Treasury bond purchases increased because speculation about credit tightening in the United States faded in the market around that time, especially after the release of U.S. payrolls data.
Net purchases of foreign bonds by Japanese investors totalled 1.2004 trillion yen in August compared with net buying of 188.4 billion yen in July, the ministry said earlier.

"Total buying in August was not big compared with July, but total sales volume decreased sharply from July, which made the net (foreign bond) purchasing volume rise," the official said. However he said the trend might not have continued in September.
